holidays.name: National Nachos Day
holidays.description: A salute to the glorious pile of crispy tortilla chips, molten cheese, jalapeños and whatever else you can balance on top. Today is a good day to build a towering tray and share it, or not.
holidays.origin: The holiday is an unofficial food observance. The dish itself was invented around 1943 in Piedras Negras, Mexico, when maître d' Ignacio "Nacho" Anaya improvised a snack of fried tortillas, melted cheese and pickled jalapeños for a group of hungry guests.
holidays.funFact: The name comes from the nickname of the inventor, Ignacio Anaya. His original recipe was called "Nacho's especiales".

holidays.name: National Basketball Day
holidays.description: A day for dribbling, shooting and slam-dunking. Lace up your sneakers, shoot some hoops, or play a round of knockout with friends.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates one of the world's most popular sports.
holidays.funFact: Basketball was invented in 1891 by Canadian-American teacher James Naismith. The first games used peach baskets, and someone had to retrieve the ball by hand after every score.

holidays.name: National Ladies Learning Code Day
holidays.description: A day that encourages women and girls to dive into the world of programming. It's a chance to write a first line of code, try a beginner workshop, or cheer on someone who is learning.
holidays.origin: The day is an unofficial observance inspired by Ladies Learning Code, a Canadian grassroots initiative founded in 2011. It began by running beginner-friendly coding workshops for women and later grew into the national nonprofit Canada Learning Code.
holidays.funFact: The initiative started as a handful of volunteer-led workshops in Toronto. It later grew to reach many thousands of learners across Canada.
